title: "Comparing CDIs for Assessing Bilingual Children"

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

require(tidyverse)
require(kableExtra)
require(mirt)
require(mirtCAT)
require(ggpubr)
```

When deciding how to assess bilingual children, researchers now have several options, including:
 - full CDI in each language
 - Swadesh-CDI in each language
 - CDI-CATs (for available languages)
 - published short forms (for available languages)
 - DLL-ES (only for English and Spanish)

The question is: what is the best option (or combination), if the goal is to assess children's ability in each language?
We compare each measure's correlation with full-CDI IRT theta, separately for English and Spanish.

```{r load-data}
# BiLexPo data -- words only, two bilingual datasets
# definition = WS_<item_id>, which matches the naming used in the IRT models.
# item_id is a per-language index (EN item 1 ≠ SP item 1), so we build
# separate EN and SP matrices rather than a single wide matrix.
bi_dat <- readRDS("data/bilingual_item_data_clean.Rds") |>
  filter(item_kind == "word") |>
  mutate(definition = paste0("WS_", item_id)) |>
  filter(dataset_origin_name %in%
           c("Marchman Dallas Bilingual", "Hoff_English_Mexican_Bilingual")) |>
  filter(production != 0, production != 680)  # remove floor and ceiling

items    <- bi_dat |>
  distinct(language, item_id, uni_lemma, english_gloss, definition, item_definition)
en_items <- items |> filter(language == "English (American)")
sp_items <- items |> filter(language == "Spanish (Mexican)")

# One row per (language × administration); production = total words produced
d_demo <- bi_dat |>
  select(language, data_id, child_id, dataset_origin_name, form, age, sex, produces) |>
  group_by(language, data_id, child_id, dataset_origin_name, form, age, sex) |>
  summarise(production = sum(produces, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(data_id)

en_idx <- which(d_demo$language == "English (American)")
sp_idx <- which(d_demo$language == "Spanish (Mexican)")

d_demo_en <- d_demo[en_idx, ]
d_demo_sp <- d_demo[sp_idx, ]

# Separate wide matrices per language (WS_<item_id> columns; rows match d_demo_en/sp)
d_mat_en <- bi_dat |>
  filter(language == "English (American)") |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = data_id, names_from = definition, values_from = produces) |>
  arrange(data_id)

d_mat_sp <- bi_dat |>
  filter(language == "Spanish (Mexican)") |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = data_id, names_from = definition, values_from = produces) |>
  arrange(data_id)
```

Using data from `r nrow(d_demo_en)` English WS administrations and `r nrow(d_demo_sp)` Spanish WS administrations.

```{r build-matrices}
# Raw item-response matrices for each language (WS_<item_id> columns, no data_id).
# Column names already match en/sp$coefs$definition, so no renaming needed.
en_dmat <- d_mat_en |> select(all_of(en_items$definition)) |> as.matrix()
sp_dmat <- d_mat_sp |> select(all_of(sp_items$definition)) |> as.matrix()

# Guard: WG administrations may use a three-level coding (0 = neither,
# 1 = understands, 2 = produces).  Collapse to strict 0/1 so fscores() and
# mirtCAT() don't reject any values outside [0, 1].
binarize <- function(m) { m[!is.na(m)] <- as.numeric(m[!is.na(m)] > 0); m }
en_dmat <- binarize(en_dmat)
sp_dmat <- binarize(sp_dmat)

# fscores() and mirtCAT() need a column for every item in the model.
# Items absent from the bilingual form get NA (= not administered).
# model_items: en$coefs$definition or sp$coefs$definition (WS_<item_id> strings)
expand_to_model <- function(dmat, model_items) {
  dmat_full <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(dmat),
                      ncol = length(model_items),
                      dimnames = list(NULL, model_items))
  shared <- intersect(colnames(dmat), model_items)
  if (length(shared) > 0)
    dmat_full[, shared] <- dmat[, shared, drop = FALSE]
  dmat_full
}
```

```{r load-irt-models}
# en$model / sp$model: fitted 2PL mirt objects
# en$coefs / sp$coefs: tibble[n_items × 5] with columns definition | a1 | d | g | u
#   where definition = WS_<item_id> matching the columns in d_mat_en / d_mat_sp
en <- readRDS("models/English (American)_2PL_allforms_prod_fits.rds")
sp <- readRDS("models/Spanish (Mexican)_2PL_allforms_prod_fits.rds")

en_model_items <- en$coefs$definition   # WS_1 … WS_682
sp_model_items <- sp$coefs$definition   # WS_1 … WS_742

# Verify bilingual items are found in the respective model
cat(sprintf("EN: %d / %d bilingual items matched to model  (%d model items total)\n",
            sum(en_items$definition %in% en_model_items),
            nrow(en_items), length(en_model_items)))
cat(sprintf("SP: %d / %d bilingual items matched to model  (%d model items total)\n",
            sum(sp_items$definition %in% sp_model_items),
            nrow(sp_items), length(sp_model_items)))

# Expand to full model item set
en_dmat_full <- expand_to_model(en_dmat, en_model_items)
sp_dmat_full <- expand_to_model(sp_dmat, sp_model_items)

# ── Full CDI theta (gold standard) ──────────────────────────────────────────
en_theta <- fscores(en$model, response.pattern = en_dmat_full, method = "MAP")
sp_theta <- fscores(sp$model, response.pattern = sp_dmat_full, method = "MAP")

d_demo_en$fullCDItheta <- en_theta[, "G"] # G not F1?
d_demo_sp$fullCDItheta <- sp_theta[, "G"]

# ── CAT simulation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Age-based start items.  The CSV was built for a different model, so the
# stored `index` values are stale.  We recover the correct index by:
#   1. joining on item_definition to get the WS_<id> definition string
#   2. calling match() to find its 1-based position in the *current* model's
#      item ordering (en/sp_model_items = en/sp$coefs$definition).
# Items whose word isn't in the bilingual subset get NA → get_start_items()
# falls back to "MI" (maximum-information first item) for those ages.
en_start_items <- read_csv("models/EN_production_start_items_by_age.csv",
                           show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(item_definition = definition) |>
  left_join(en_items |> select(item_definition, definition, uni_lemma),
            by = "item_definition") |>
  mutate(index = match(definition, en_model_items))

sp_start_items <- read_csv("models/SP_production_start_items_by_age.csv",
                           show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(item_definition = definition) |>
  left_join(sp_items |> select(item_definition, definition, uni_lemma),
            by = "item_definition") |>
  mutate(index = match(definition, sp_model_items))

# ── IRT-based imputation of missing items ───────────────────────────────────
# mirtCAT reads a "true" response from local_pattern for every item it selects.
# Items absent from the bilingual form are NA → mirtCAT errors.  We fill those
# NAs with the rounded P(X=1 | θ_i) from the 2PL model so the CAT has a valid
# response for any item it might choose.
# coefs tibble must have columns: definition, a1, d, g, u
impute_2pl <- function(dmat_full, coefs, theta_vec) {
  dmat_imp <- dmat_full
  na_cols  <- which(apply(dmat_full, 2, anyNA))
  if (length(na_cols) == 0) return(dmat_imp)

  for (j in na_cols) {
    p <- coefs[coefs$definition == colnames(dmat_full)[j], ]
    if (nrow(p) == 0) next
    na_rows <- which(is.na(dmat_full[, j]))
    prob <- p$g[1] + (p$u[1] - p$g[1]) /
              (1 + exp(-(p$a1[1] * theta_vec[na_rows] + p$d[1])))
    dmat_imp[na_rows, j] <- round(prob)
  }
  dmat_imp
}

en_dmat_full_imp <- impute_2pl(en_dmat_full, en$coefs, d_demo_en$fullCDItheta)
sp_dmat_full_imp <- impute_2pl(sp_dmat_full, sp$coefs, d_demo_sp$fullCDItheta)

cat(sprintf("EN NAs remaining after imputation: %d\n", sum(is.na(en_dmat_full_imp))))
cat(sprintf("SP NAs remaining after imputation: %d\n", sum(is.na(sp_dmat_full_imp))))

# ── CAT simulation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simulate adaptive testing using each child's actual + imputed responses as
# ground truth.  Stops when SEM < min_SEM (or after min_items–max_items items).
preferredCAT <- function(mod, dat, method = "MAP", min_SEM = .15,
                         start_item = c()) {
  if (length(start_item) == 0) start_item <- "MI"
  results <- mirtCAT(mo = mod, criteria = "MI", start_item = start_item,
                     method = method, local_pattern = dat,
                     design = list(min_items = 25, max_items = 50,
                                   min_SEM = min_SEM))
  parms <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(results), function(s) {
    so <- summary(results[[s]])
    c(t(so$final_estimates), length(so$items_answered))
  }))
  parms <- as.data.frame(parms)
  names(parms) <- c("thetaCAT", "CAT_SE", "Qs_asked")
  parms
}

# Map each subject's age to the recommended start item index in the model
get_start_items <- function(ages, start_df) {
  sapply(ages, function(a) {
    idx <- start_df |> filter(age == a) |> slice(1) |> pull(index)
    if (length(idx) == 0 || is.na(idx)) "MI" else idx
  })
}

en_start_subj <- get_start_items(d_demo_en$age, en_start_items)
sp_start_subj <- get_start_items(d_demo_sp$age, sp_start_items)


# Also inspect the start_item vector
cat("en_start_subj unique values:", sort(unique(en_start_subj)), "\n")
cat("  (any 'MI'?", any(en_start_subj == "MI"), ")\n")

en_cat <- preferredCAT(en$model, en_dmat_full_imp, start_item = en_start_subj)
sp_cat <- preferredCAT(sp$model, sp_dmat_full_imp, start_item = sp_start_subj)

d_demo_en$CATtheta <- en_cat$thetaCAT
d_demo_en$CAT_SE   <- en_cat$CAT_SE
d_demo_en$Qs_asked <- en_cat$Qs_asked

d_demo_sp$CATtheta <- sp_cat$thetaCAT
d_demo_sp$CAT_SE   <- sp_cat$CAT_SE
d_demo_sp$Qs_asked <- sp_cat$Qs_asked

cat(sprintf("Median CAT items asked — EN: %.0f  SP: %.0f\n",
            median(en_cat$Qs_asked), median(sp_cat$Qs_asked)))
```

```{r load-forms}
swad100 <- read_csv("forms/Swadesh100.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

swad_extension_unis <- c(
  "try", "under", "in", "out",
  "glue (object)", "toy (object)",
  "all", "many", "not", "a lot"
)
swad110 <- tibble(uni_lemma = c(swad100$uni_lemma, swad_extension_unis))

# Floccia et al. (2020) 30-item cross-linguistic short form (English glosses)
floccia30_en <- c("elephant", "fish (animal)", "lion", "airplane", "car", "ball",
                  "book", "milk", "nose", "shoe", "sock", "bed", "chair", "door",
                  "table", "cup", "scissors", "soap", "flower", "sky", "tree",
                  "mommy", "fall (action)", "play", "big", "cold", "dirty", "hot",
                  "what", "where (question)")

en_shortA <- read_csv("forms/eng-ws-shortA.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
en_shortB <- read_csv("forms/eng-ws-shortB.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
sp_short  <- read_csv("forms/spanish-ws-short.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

dll2long_raw <- read_csv("forms/DLL/new_DLL-ES2-long.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> 
  select(-`...1`)
dll2long <- dll2long_raw |>
  mutate(english = tolower(english)) |>
  mutate(english = case_when(
    english == "daddy (or name/word used in your family)" ~ "daddy*",
    english == "teddy bear"                              ~ "teddybear",
    english == "patty cake"                              ~ "pattycake",
    english == "dress"                                   ~ "dress (object)",
    english == "i"                                       ~ "I",
    english == "penis (or word used in your family)"     ~ "penis*",
    english == "water"                                   ~ "water (beverage)",
    english == "orange"                                  ~ "orange (food)",
    english == "clock/watch"                             ~ "clock",
    english == "drink"                                   ~ "drink (action)",
    english == "feet"                                    ~ "foot",
    english == 'picture ("or photo")'                   ~ "picture",
    english == "buttocks/bottom (or word used in your family)" ~
      "buttocks/bottom*",
    TRUE ~ english
  )) |>
  mutate(spanish = tolower(spanish)) |>
  separate(col = spanish, into = c("spanish", NA), sep = " \\(") |>
  mutate(spanish = case_when(
    spanish == "pipi"  ~ "pipí",
    spanish == "shh"   ~ "shhh",
    spanish == "bolsa" ~ "bolsa (clothing)",
    spanish == "qué"   ~ "qué (question_words)",
    TRUE ~ spanish
  ))
```

```{r score-forms}
# ── Helpers: map human-readable form word lists → WS_<id> column names ──────
# Look up item_definition (or uni_lemma) in en_items / sp_items to get the
# WS_<id> definition strings present as columns in d_mat_en / d_mat_sp.
match_en <- function(words) {
  en_items |> filter(item_definition %in% words) |>
    pull(definition) |> intersect(colnames(d_mat_en))
}
match_sp <- function(words) {
  sp_items |> filter(item_definition %in% words) |>
    pull(definition) |> intersect(colnames(d_mat_sp))
}
match_uni_en <- function(unis) {
  en_items |> filter(uni_lemma %in% unis) |>
    pull(definition) |> intersect(colnames(d_mat_en))
}
match_uni_sp <- function(unis) {
  sp_items |> filter(uni_lemma %in% unis) |>
    pull(definition) |> intersect(colnames(d_mat_sp))
}

# ── Locate item columns for each form ───────────────────────────────────────
shortA_en_cols  <- match_en(en_shortA$word)
short_sp_cols   <- match_sp(sp_short$word)

swad100_en_cols <- match_uni_en(swad100$uni_lemma)
swad100_sp_cols <- match_uni_sp(swad100$uni_lemma)

dll2_en_cols    <- match_en(dll2long$english)
dll2_sp_cols    <- match_sp(dll2long$spanish)

# Floccia: English glosses → shared uni_lemmas → SP definitions
floccia_unis    <- en_items |> filter(item_definition %in% floccia30_en) |> pull(uni_lemma)
floccia_en_cols <- match_uni_en(floccia_unis)
floccia_sp_cols <- match_uni_sp(floccia_unis)

# ── Item coverage table ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
tibble(
  Form          = c("EN shortA", "SP short",
                    "Swadesh-100 EN", "Swadesh-100 SP",
                    "DLL-ES2 EN", "DLL-ES2 SP",
                    "Floccia-30 EN", "Floccia-30 SP"),
  Items_matched = c(length(shortA_en_cols),  length(short_sp_cols),
                    length(swad100_en_cols),  length(swad100_sp_cols),
                    length(dll2_en_cols),     length(dll2_sp_cols),
                    length(floccia_en_cols),  length(floccia_sp_cols)),
  Form_total    = c(nrow(en_shortA), nrow(sp_short),
                    100, 100,
                    nrow(dll2long), nrow(dll2long),
                    length(floccia30_en), length(floccia30_en))
) |>
  mutate(Pct_matched = round(100 * Items_matched / Form_total)) |>
  kable(caption = "Item coverage: bilingual data vs. each form") |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

# ── Compute sum scores (directly into the per-language demo frames) ──────────
d_demo_en$shortForm_sum <- rowSums(d_mat_en[, shortA_en_cols,  drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
d_demo_en$swad100_sum   <- rowSums(d_mat_en[, swad100_en_cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
d_demo_en$dll2_sum      <- rowSums(d_mat_en[, dll2_en_cols,    drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
d_demo_en$floccia_sum   <- rowSums(d_mat_en[, floccia_en_cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)

d_demo_sp$shortForm_sum <- rowSums(d_mat_sp[, short_sp_cols,   drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
d_demo_sp$swad100_sum   <- rowSums(d_mat_sp[, swad100_sp_cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
d_demo_sp$dll2_sum      <- rowSums(d_mat_sp[, dll2_sp_cols,    drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
d_demo_sp$floccia_sum   <- rowSums(d_mat_sp[, floccia_sp_cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Bakeoff: correlation with full-CDI θ

For each measure we compute Pearson *r* with the full-CDI MAP theta estimate,
separately for English and Spanish.
The CDI-CAT is the IRT-based adaptive alternative; all others are sum scores.

```{r bakeoff, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
measures       <- c("shortForm_sum", "swad100_sum", "dll2_sum", "floccia_sum", "CATtheta")
measure_labels <- c("Published\nShort Form", "Swadesh-100",
                    "DLL-ES2", "Floccia-30", "CDI-CAT")

# Combine for plotting, then compute correlations within each language
d_bakeoff <- bind_rows(
  d_demo_en |> mutate(lang = "English"),
  d_demo_sp |> mutate(lang = "Spanish")
)

cor_table <- d_bakeoff |>
  group_by(lang) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(measures),
                   ~ cor(.x, fullCDItheta, use = "complete.obs")),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(measures), names_to = "measure", values_to = "r") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measures, labels = measure_labels))

# ── Summary table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cor_table |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = lang, values_from = r) |>
  rename(Measure = measure) |>
  kable(digits = 3,
        caption = "Correlation with full-CDI θ (MAP) by language") |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

# ── Bar chart ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cor_table |>
  ggplot(aes(x = measure, y = r, fill = lang)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(.7), width = .6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", r)),
            position = position_dodge(.7), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("English" = "#4575b4", "Spanish" = "#d73027")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.85, 1.0)) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = expression(italic(r) ~ "with full-CDI" ~ theta),
       fill = NULL,
       title = "CDI bakeoff: correlation with full-CDI θ by language") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r bakeoff-scatter, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
# Scatter plots: full-CDI theta vs. each measure, faceted by language
d_bakeoff |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(measures), names_to = "measure", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measures, labels = measure_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fullCDItheta, y = score, color = lang)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .25, size = .8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = .8) +
  facet_grid(lang ~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("English" = "#4575b4", "Spanish" = "#d73027"),
                     guide = "none") +
  labs(x = expression("Full-CDI" ~ theta ~ "(MAP)"),
       y = "Measure score",
       title = "Full-CDI θ vs. each reduced-form measure") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```
